newsitem.title: USA: Ukraine gas firm says prime minister not an investor.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine gas firm says prime minister not an investor.

text.p: The chief executive of a Ukrainian energy importing company on Monday denied a report that Ukrainian Prime Minister Pavlo Lazarenko has a stake in the company.

"He has no shares. It's impossible," Yulia Tymoshenko, president of United Energy Systems of Ukraine (UESU), said through an interpreter at a briefing sponsored by the Johns Hopkins School of International Relations.

The New York Times in an article last week on Ukrainian government corruption said Western intelligence sources said Lazarenko has an interest in UESU, which has a license to import natural gas and oil.
The article said Lazarenko is one of a number of Ukrainian officials who, according to its business and diplomatic sources, have profited from private business dealings while holding public office.

A number of reports also have circulated that UESU, which delivers energy partly by importing Russian natural gas in exchange for exported commodities, has benefited from special favours from government officials.
But Tymoshenko dismissed those reports, saying that the company has avoided debts to Russia and promoted Ukraine's independence, "and not everyone is pleased with that."

To gain energy independence from Russia, she said Ukraine will need investments from the United States and other western powers. But she said hardline conservatives are blocking market reforms Ukraine needs to encourage investment and build a viable economy.

Elected to Ukraine's parliament last year, Tymoshenko said she will push legislation to reform private property laws and encourage investment which she said would reduce the "influence of the bureaucracy and the shadow economy on business."
She also said a conference of U.S. and Ukrainian business and government officials will be held in June in Kiev on making Ukraine more lucrative for U.S. investors.
"The first step should be an open dialogue and no efforts to hide information," she said.
